intent: Show that median SAT scores rise steadily as family income increases across the seven income brackets.

requirements.question: How do median SAT scores change across the seven family-income brackets?

units.claim: Median SAT scores rise at every successive income bracket.
accept: each income-bracket bar is taller than the preceding income-bracket bar
reject: claiming a complete seven-bracket trend when any income-bracket bar is missing
any decline or non-increasing step in the sequence
claiming that the displayed data establish a causal effect of income on SAT scores; the source only shows an association
units.evidence: Seven horizontal bars are present for the seven income brackets, and every successive bar is longer than the previous one.

optional_valid: The narration calls the values average scores, while the chart title specifies median scores.

g0_data_completeness.selection: all data rows because the table has no role column
